0x0F5.detail: Set with 0x0FF and 0x0FE when the whole party drops out of view: the fall into the river (npc/1), the Zephyr nap and storm (npc/42), the Picard recovery (npc/9) and Darkbeat's flight from God's Tower (npc/30); cleared when $C is back, e.g. 'Wake up $A' on Kerple (npc/19). In Picard while it is set, $C's rest offers and Ibkee's translated hint don't play, beds only say 'A bed.' and Darkbeat asks where $B and $C are. Engine code also reads it.
0x0F5.engine: Nehani is away. While set, the field menu greys out and refuses the 'Nehani' row, Nehani's floating sprite and sparkle trail aren't drawn (checked at map load), and a full-inventory chest says "You can't carry any more items" as narration instead of Nehani's "You have too many items."

0x0F6.name: all_living_toys_found
0x0F6.detail: No script sets it (engine code does). On Zeppetto Island (npc/36) Zeppetto Jr. checks it: when set he asks to see all of your Living Toys, the ghost of Professor Zeppetto gives item 1036 and leaves (0x0A3); otherwise he only remarks that 68 toys were made.
0x0F6.engine: Set by the engine when a Living Toy is given and the owned-toy bits become the complete set (all 68); Zeppetto's grandson (npc/36) tests it.

0x0F7.name: demo_only_orgo_san_claria
0x0F7.summary: Only Orgo and San Claria NPCs load (unused)
0x0F7.engine: While set, the field never starts the music/hotspot task and every chunk's NPC pack is dropped except packs 4 (San Claria) and 6 (Orgo). Nothing in the code or the scripts sets it, so it looks like a demo/debug limiter.

0x0F8.name: no_flag
0x0F8.detail: Setting 0x0F8 does nothing, so 283 of 291 chests use it as 'no flag', including every NPC gift scripted as chest flag:0x0F8 (Amos's map, Zeppetto's toy, the Recruiter's reward). Scripts never set or test it directly.
0x0F8.engine: Dummy flag: SetEventFlag returns without setting it, and the chest opcode also skips setting it, so chests and scripts use 0xF8 as 'no flag' (the chest can be opened again).

0x0F9.name: chapter_1_the_journey
0x0F9.detail: Set by Martha at Amos and Martha's inn (npc/1) right after the Baby is given its name. The save screen names the chapter from the first of 0x0AB, 0x09D, 0x086, 0x0F9 that is set.
0x0F9.engine: Almost every Baby feature needs 0xF9 plus the Baby in the party: fighting, exp, learning forms, the Baby menu row and stats, 'Let <Baby> Carry', overflow loot and carried items counting as owned. It also picks the chapter title 'The Journey' (chapter 1).

0x0FA.name: water_bug_met
0x0FA.summary: Have ridden the water bug before
0x0FA.engine: Set the first time you board the water bug (root mode 20). Until then the boarding sequence plays an extra line first (nested script 6, "It's a huge water bug!") before the usual "get on his back" line (script 7).

0x0FB.name: picard_wakeup_in_progress
0x0FB.summary: Mid-way through the Picard wake-up scenes
0x0FB.detail: Set (with scratch 0x008, while clearing 0x0F5) by one step of the Picard wake-up chain after Xizan's release (npc/9 actor 11) and cleared by the next scene, where $B reappears and 0x0FE is cleared. No script tests it; engine code reads it, so its purpose is a guess from this one use.
0x0FB.engine: While set, Nehani's sprite circles round the Knight every frame instead of trailing behind him. Set and cleared by scripts in Picard (npc/9) while the Baby is missing.

0x0FC.name: scene_music_playing
0x0FC.summary: Scene music is playing; area music held back
0x0FC.detail: Scripts set it right before sfx 0 and a new bgm when a scene takes over the music (Bonik's song, the wedding, boss intros, going to bed) and clear it, usually after bgm_fade 513, when the scene ends. New game also sets it, and engine code reads and sets it.
0x0FC.engine: While set, the overworld music manager won't change music by map zone, and waking at an inn doesn't restart the area music. A new game sets it, and scene tasks (water-bug boarding, flight, sky scene, scene setup, credits) set it and clear it when they finish.

0x0FD.name: wipe_scratch
0x0FD.detail: SET 0x0FD clears all 64 scratch flags instead of setting a bit; the DSL prints it as wipe_scratch. 111 trigger records use it to reset an area's scratch state on entry (e.g. Trisken once 0x0C1 is set), and many scene programs call it after major events.
0x0FD.engine: Pseudo-flag: SET 0xFD from a script (op 0x04) or a Tier-1 trigger record clears flags 0–63 (the scratch band) instead of setting a bit. Choosing 'Fly' from the Baby menu wipes the band too.

0x0FE.name: baby_not_with_party
0x0FE.summary: Baby is not following the Knight
0x0FE.detail: New game sets it. Scripts set it whenever the Baby leaves or is staged as a scene actor (left at the Cave of Fear in npc/1, left outside a café in npc/34, lost in the Zephyr storm in npc/42, the God's Tower and Picard scenes) and clear it when the Baby rejoins, e.g. after the Kell bird fight (npc/40) or once Yugonga falls on Kerple (npc/18).
